ذَهَبَ دَمُهُ خِضْرًا مِضْرًا , (S, A, K,) and خَضِرًا ↓ مَضِرًا , (K,) His blood went unrevenged, or unretaliated, or unexpiated by a mulct: (S, K:) or so as to occasion no inconvenience or trouble (هَنِيْئًا مَرِيْئًا) to the slayer: (A:) مضرا is an imitative sequent: Ks mentions also بِضْرًا, with ب. (S.) ―
-b2- You say also, خُذْهُ خِضْرًا مِضْرًا, (K, TA,) and ↓ خَضِرًا مَضِرًا , (Sgh, TA, and so in the CK,) Take thou it in a fresh, or juicy, state. (K.) See also art. خضر.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
